set.approach: Upper Provo Falls is reached from the highway up Provo Canyon by turning south at the Upper Falls parking sign, a mile or so past the Nunn's Park lot, and driving to the gate where the plowed road ends. From the gate, follow the road down to the first bridge over the river; once across, the trail starts behind the concrete structures on the far side of the paved path. The flow is in the high upper basin, just right of Frigid Perculator. Follow the approach used for FMR, climbing several short WI3 steps; after the first pitch and the low-angle ice above it, bear right up the creek. The drainage forks, and the left branch opens into a larger basin where this flow and Frigid Perculator stand above one more short WI3 step. The ice here sits under avalanche start zones that are hard to see from below, so check the avalanche forecast.

set.approach: Park at the top of 29th Street and take the trail up and around to the south into the first major canyon. Cross a small bridge and continue up the drainage, with the trail on its north side, until the flow comes into view at the head of the canyon.
set.descent_text: Either rappel the route or walk off. Rappels use pin anchors, and V-thread materials are worth carrying in case. To walk off, continue up the drainage above the frozen pool, then gain the ridgeline directly to the east; the trail drops steeply back into the canyon you started in, higher up than where packs were left.

review.notes: Area and route pages (one lineage). Approach time and rappel count deliberately left out.

set.approach: Upper Provo Falls is reached from the highway up Provo Canyon by turning south at the Upper Falls parking sign, a mile or so past the Nunn's Park lot, and driving to the gate where the plowed road ends. From the gate, follow the road down to the first bridge over the river; once across, the trail starts behind the concrete structures on the far side of the paved path. The trail continues up Avalanche Canyon from behind the concrete structure. The first pitch is a WI3 section with a graffiti-covered amphitheater on the left. Continue up the west (right-hand) drainage on many steps of WI2-3 to a WI4 pillar and curtain, then trend right through a steep wooded slope to the last headwall. This is a major avalanche path, so check the avalanche forecast before climbing or approaching.
set.descent_text: Descend from slings on trees, walking and downclimbing around the steeper sections through the trees. Bring tat for V-threads and two 60 m ropes for the rappels.
